data.rule: In a ddflow checkout, agents append to committed .ddflow/events/*.jsonl continuously, so any tool that diffs the working tree before and after a step (pre-commit's 'files were modified by this hook', a formatter's --check on the whole tree, a 'git status is clean' assertion) fails there at random, and the longer the step the likelier. Run such checks in a scratch worktree of the commit under test (git worktree add --detach), which has no other writers and also tests the commit rather than uncommitted state.
data.title: A check that watches the working tree cannot run where other processes write it

data.summary: heartbeat revives an EXPIRED lease with its claim-time globs: update --globs on an item whose lease has lapsed changes item.globs only (plan_retarget leaves an expired lease for recovery), and the later heartbeat renews the lease without them, so the commit hook reports the paths just added as not covered. Reproduced: claim T5 i/* (ttl 2 s, grace 1 s), wait, update --globs i/*,j/*, heartbeat -> lease globs [i/*]; check-commit: j/f not covered. Seen live on B-prepush-isolated (demos/, pyproject.toml).

data.claim: Review time is the reviewer's reasoning length, which is random per call, multiplied by sequentially-sent chunks; the LAN vLLM server is idle and has capacity for many parallel requests
data.falsifier: server queueing or prefill dominating; or reasoning length stable across runs of the same input; or throughput collapsing under concurrency
data.mechanism: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decodes ~10 ms/token single-stream (vLLM metrics: ITL 11 ms, TTFT 0.1 s, queue 3 ms); one review chunk generates 6k-42k reasoning tokens at temperature 1.0; ddflow sends chunks of max_chunk_chars=5000 one after another; roborev (kilo agent loop) spends most of a job in one final reasoning call
